# Round 1: Cauchy completeness escalation

Confirmed defect `f44-six-b3-cauchy-lub-bridge`: the original last proof step did not establish the least-upper-bound portion of the unchanged Statement. The repaired carrier supplies deterministic bisection, proves shrinking widths from already declared rational Archimedeanity, obtains the lower-endpoint limit from Cauchy completeness, traps that limit in every interval and proves both upper-bound inequalities. The natural recursion and induction suppliers are explicit. The original rational selector remains choice-free; the bisection rule selects no family of witnesses. No dependency on the later corollary is introduced. This preserves the richer approved claim at the cost of five additional proof rows.

Root proof review of thm-reals-cauchy-complete

The original six-step Cauchy construction is retained. I read the complete eleven-step repaired carrier. The new bisection self-map uniquely chooses the half interval according to whether its midpoint is an upper bound, so recursion uses no countable choice. Its invariant is that each lower endpoint is not an upper bound and each upper endpoint is an upper bound. The width is w/2^k; one rational upper bound on w and 2^k >= k+1 reduce shrinking to rational Archimedeanity. Nestedness makes lower endpoints Cauchy; the already proved Cauchy completeness gives their limit. Order-density epsilon contradictions put that limit in every interval and prove convergence of upper endpoints. Each member of S lies below every upper endpoint, hence below the limit. Every upper bound lies above every lower endpoint, hence above the limit. This proves exactly the missing LUB property while preserving the original complete-field Statement and avoiding the corollary reverse dependency. Only one initial member of S and one upper bound are fixed existentially; no family of witnesses is chosen.

This is the authorized owner resolution following the native batch-3 escalation, not a new engine worker receipt or whole-library audit. The original independent decision is archived alongside this record, and the recorded-local-published-repair receipt authenticates actual pre-edit ownership and local checks.

+1.2 To prove the least-upper-bound property, fix any nonempty $S\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ and any upper bound $U$. Fix one $t_0\in S$, and set $u_0=t_0-1$, $v_0=U$. Then $u_0$ is not an upper bound, $v_0$ is an upper bound, and $u_0<v_0$. For any pair $(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, put $m=(u+v)/2$ and send $(u,v)$ to $(u,m)$ if $m$ is an upper bound of $S$, and to $(m,v)$ otherwise. This specifies a single self-map; [L9] gives its unique iterated sequence $(u_k,v_k)_{k\ge0}$. Only one element $t_0$ and one upper bound are fixed; each later value is uniquely determined, so no choice axiom is used. [L4, L7, L8, L9, construct]
+
 2.1 Let $h_k$ be the least first coordinate of an admissible triple; with $h_k$ fixed, let $b_k$ be the least admissible second coordinate; with both fixed, let $j_k$ be the least admissible third coordinate. Each minimum exists and is unique by [L7]. Define $q_k=(j_k-h_k)/b_k$. This unique rule defines the graph of $(q_k)$ as a subset of $\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}\times\mathbb{Q}$ by Separation. +
+2.2 Induction gives that $u_k$ is not an upper bound, $v_k$ is an upper bound, $u_k\le u_{k+1}\le v_{k+1}\le v_k$, and $v_k-u_k=(v_0-u_0)/2^k$. Here $2^0=1$ and $2^{k+1}=2\cdot2^k$, defined by recursion. Also $2^k\ge k+1$: the base case is equality, and $2(k+1)\ge k+2$ propagates the bound. Put $w=v_0-u_0>0$.
